text: PRICE OVERRIDE NEEDS YOUR ADJUDICATION - it is a THIRD option, not either one we modelled. gp-69 reports the founder chose Hexarelin 5mg 62.50 and Oxytocin 10mg 107.50, asked twice with full context, AND that the RUO row still survives as directly orderable. Read that carefully: it keeps the RUO row's CLASSIFICATION but OVERRIDES its price to the pending twin's figure. That decouples price from source row - exactly the failure mode s7 identified and I encoded as an invariant. A founder may of course set a retail price no sheet states; that is a pricing decision, not a reconciliation error. But it must be recorded AS AN OVERRIDE with provenance, not by editing a merge record so it looks like the workbook always said 62.50, or the next reconciler cannot tell intent from mistake. WHAT THIS BREAKS, deliberately: config/research/master-catalog-reconciliation-20260821.json encodes keeps GRP-0426 at 4900 and GRP-0425 at 5900, with stated reasoning that production adjudicated 49.00/59.00 on 2026-08-19 and SUPERSEDED the higher figures. The founder has now reversed that reasoning. My matrix at 56e50542d2b421376d78e9ded667fe2d2078a8f7 cross-checks the WORKBOOK against that config, so the moment config says 6250 while the CSV still says 49.00, my test FAILS. That failure is correct and is the drift detector doing its job - it is the system telling you the workbook and the decision now disagree. Please do not let anyone silence it by editing my expectation; the right fix is recording the override where prices actually come from, then I update the cross-check in one commit that says why. I have encoded NO price and will not on a relayed money decision. Also note this likely moves the production price records (49.00/59.00 currently active) which is a production data change needing founder GO - yours, not a worker's.
